title: Week 2: from DigiCash to UTXOs
summary: The first discussion round of our Decoding Bitcoin cohort. Six people explained the six week 1 questions: why earlier digital cash failed, the Genesis block and Pizza Day, hash functions, UTXOs as notes in a wallet, and don't trust, verify. Plus Razor and Alex on the BOSS Challenge.
share_text: Decoding Bitcoin week 2: why b-money's voting breaks with fake nodes, 10,000 BTC for two pizzas, paint you can't unmix, and UTXOs as notes in your wallet. Notes and 4 mini-games from @CodeOrangeDevs

Want the deep end? Try Saving Satoshi, the entry test for the BOSS Challenge.

tldr: Bitcoin was not the first try at digital cash. DigiCash needed one company, b-money and Bit Gold stayed on paper. Satoshi combined proof of work with "follow the chain with the most work", so fake nodes can't outvote the honest ones.
History you can check yourself: the Genesis block, 10 BTC to Hal Finney, 10,000 BTC for two pizzas, and Satoshi's last email: "I've moved on to other things."
A hash is paint you can't unmix: same input, same output, no way back, and no two inputs with the same result. UTXOs are notes in your wallet: you hand over a whole note and get change back.
Want the deep end? The BOSS Challenge is a recruitment pipeline for Bitcoin developers, and Saving Satoshi is the way in. Decoding Bitcoin stays beginner friendly.

ideas: Also on the call: Alex and Andy had just come back from the three-day Bitcoin Educator Academy in Chiang Mai (public speaking for Bitcoin educators), and the day before the call a hangout at the Bitcoin Learning Center tried bitchat, White Noise, Fedi federations and a multi-vendor multisig. An open question to research: did Satoshi pick UTXOs by design, or could Bitcoin have worked with accounts? One person flagged that later weeks in the weekly plan are still locked; keypleb is making every week visible.

quiz.q: Why could b-money's "majority vote" not stop a double spend?
o: Votes were too slow to count
An attacker can spin up a thousand fake nodes and outvote everyone
It had no way to send money at all
quiz.w: Votes are cheap to fake. Bitcoin's vote is proof of work: to rewrite history you need real energy, not more nodes.

quiz.q: You pay 0.3 BTC from a single 0.5 BTC UTXO. What happens?
o: 0.3 BTC is cut off the old UTXO, which stays in your wallet
The whole 0.5 is spent, and two new outputs appear: 0.3 to them, about 0.2 back to you as change
Your account balance goes down by 0.3
quiz.w: Like paying with a banknote. The old UTXO is spent for good and change comes back as a new one (minus a small fee).

quiz.q: Which property means you can't work out the input from a hash?
quiz.w: Like mixing black into white paint: you get grey and can never unmix it.

quiz.q: Where is your Bitcoin balance stored?
o: In a balance field on the blockchain
Nowhere: your wallet adds up the UTXOs your keys can spend
At the exchange you bought it from
quiz.w: The chain only records which coins exist and who can spend them. The total is your wallet doing the sum.
